subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-agent delegate-only tool policy such as tools.selfDeny, or should this use case be handled only through per-spawn child restrictions and separate agent profiles?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent config key, deny precedence, inherited policy model, and relationship to toolsAllow are security/API choices that automation should not settle.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Use only per-spawn controls
options.body: Treat toolsAllow-style child narrowing as the supported path and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate profiles or agent configuration.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance
options.body: Reject delegate-only escalation for now and document that a parent cannot pass tools it cannot itself receive under the current model.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.
